def Target : Prop :=
  let K : ArithmeticSentence → ArithmeticSentence := fun σ => (𝗣𝗔 : ArithmeticTheory).standardProvability σ
  let F : ArithmeticSentence → ArithmeticSentence := K
  let 𝓢 : ArithmeticTheory := 𝗣𝗔 ∪ (𝗣𝗔 : ArithmeticTheory).localReflectionOn Set.univ
  Def1 (𝗣𝗔 : ArithmeticTheory) K ∧ (𝗣𝗔 : ArithmeticTheory) ⪯ 𝓢 ∧
    Def2 𝓢 K ∧ Def3 𝓢 K ∧
    Def5 (𝗣𝗔 : ArithmeticTheory) F ∧
    (∀ φ, 𝓢 ⊢ K (K φ 🡘 F φ)) ∧
    (∃ p, 𝓢 ⊢ K (K (∼p) 🡘 p)) ∧
    Entailment.Consistent 𝓢 ∧
    Def4 𝓢 K

With these choices fixed, Target is the conjunction of the following requirements, in order. All sentence variables range over closed arithmetic sentences. (1) For every φ, if PA proves φ, then PA proves K(φ). (2) For every sentence, if PA proves it, then 𝓢 proves it. (3) For every φ and every ψ, 𝓢 proves the sentence K(φ → ψ) → (K(φ) → K(ψ)). translation: Target defines a proposition; it does not assert that the proposition holds. Fix K(σ) to be the arithmetic sentence Prov_PA(⌜σ⌝), let F be that very same function K, and let 𝓢 be PA together with all axioms K(σ) → σ, one for every arithmetic sentence σ. With these choices fixed, Target is the conjunction of the following requirements, in order. All sentence variables range over closed arithmetic sentences. (1) For every φ, if PA proves φ, then PA proves K(φ). (2) For every sentence, if PA proves it, then 𝓢 proves it. (3) For every φ and every ψ, 𝓢 proves the sentence K(φ → ψ) → (K(φ) → K(ψ)). (4) For every φ, 𝓢 proves K(φ) → φ. (5) There exists a ψ such that PA proves ψ ↔ ¬F(ψ). (6) For every φ, 𝓢 proves K(K(φ) ↔ F(φ)). (7) There exists a p such that 𝓢 proves K(K(¬p) ↔ p). (8) 𝓢 does not prove every arithmetic sentence. (9) For every φ, 𝓢 proves K(K(φ) → φ). Each quantifier is local to its own conjunct: in particular, p need not be the witness ψ from (5), and (7) is not required for every p. In (6), (7), and (9), the outer K applies to the entire indicated biconditional or implication and denotes PA provability, even though the system required to prove the resulting sentence is 𝓢. Consistency in (8) is a conjunct, not a hypothesis for the other clauses.

divergences.description: Clause (ix) requires `¬ Def4 𝓢 K`, but the TARGET ends with `Def4 𝓢 K`. It requires 𝓢 to prove `K (K φ 🡒 φ)` for every arithmetic sentence φ, exactly what (ix) denies.

judgement.summary: The definitions of K, F, and 𝓢 and clauses (i)–(viii) match the author's claim. The sole divergence is the missing negation in (ix).
